purpose: Phase 9 BOUNDEDNESS HARDENING pass, Steps 4 and 6 - raw, repo-committed development-evidence distributions used to derive CLAIM_EVALUATION_BUDGET, MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_ROUND, and MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_REQUEST in research/loop_control.py. Extracted by direct read of the exact JSON artifacts named below (no live calls, no fabrication, no Phase-10 data). n<30-report-raw-values convention (PHASE9_RELIABILITY_PERFORMANCE_CONTRACT.md) followed for every distribution here.

primary_corpus.description: n_factual_claims, strictly - every value found by grepping the 3 files the governing directive explicitly named, at the (case, round) granularity Phase-8's own artifacts recorded. Each value is one generation cycle's factual-claim count (= one gap_analysis_node visit's worth of candidate judge calls).
primary_corpus.note: n=45 exceeds this project's own n<30 raw-value-reporting threshold, but the raw sorted list is still disclosed in full here for auditability; the summary stats (n/min/median/max) are what downstream docs cite.

cumulative_per_multi_round_case.description: For every (case) with >1 recorded round in the primary corpus, the SUM of n_factual_claims across all its real rounds - this is the actual request-global cumulative total a real multi-round request produced, which is what CLAIM_EVALUATION_BUDGET (a request-global budget) is most directly comparable to.
cumulative_per_multi_round_case.note: The hard MAX_RESEARCH_ITERATIONS bound allows up to 4 real rounds (G=4) - none of these dev/validation cases actually exercised more than 2, so 16 is a REAL observed floor on 'what request-global cumulative claim totals look like in practice', not a ceiling accounting for the full hard-bounded round count.

broader_corpus_including_phase6_single_s.description: n_factual_claims values ALSO found in Phase-6 (pre-research-loop, single-shot generation, no gap-analysis loop) artifacts - included for context only, NOT used as the primary basis for CLAIM_EVALUATION_BUDGET, since these answers never went through research/gap_analysis.py's judge-call loop at all (Phase 6 predates Phase 8's research loop).
broader_corpus_including_phase6_single_s.note: Confirms the primary corpus's max=8 is not an artifact of only checking 3 files - the broader corpus (54 values total) has the identical max (8).

excluded_as_not_comparable.description: artifacts/v2/phase7_*.json files also contain a field literally named 'n_claims' (not 'n_factual_claims') with values up to 32 - inspected directly (phase7_candidate_b_fresh_supplement_results.json) and confirmed this is an AGGREGATE summary field counting claims across MANY test cases in one evaluation batch, not a per-answer/per-cycle count comparable to Phase-8's per-round n_factual_claims. Excluded from the distribution above to avoid conflating aggregate-batch counts with per-request counts - documented here rather than silently dropped.

aggregate_per_request.description: n_tool_calls field from artifacts/v2/phase9_baseline_results.json's 12 real (live, Category-A) baseline cases - the TOTAL count of tool_call_history entries across the WHOLE request (all rounds combined), not a per-round breakdown.
aggregate_per_request.max_case: F5-research-loop-one-followup (12 total tool calls across its multiple rounds)

per_round_breakdown.statement: NO repo-committed artifact (phase8_*.json or phase9_*.json) records the PER-ROUND length of the model-emitted raw_tool_calls[] array specifically - grep confirmed (`tool_calls_per_round`, `n_tool_calls`, `tools_called` patterns) against every artifacts/v2/phase8_*.json file returns no per-round breakdown; phase9_baseline_results.json's n_tool_calls is an aggregate-per-request figure only. This is stated explicitly per the governing directive's instruction to say so rather than guess.

code_level_soft_ceiling_used_as_secondar.corrected_per_round_soft_ceiling_order_o: ~20-30 valid tool_calls/round, derived from orchestration/candidate_b_native_tools.py's call_cerebras_native_tools max_completion_tokens=1024 default (no override), using the same order-of-magnitude token-cost-per-entry reasoning as the claim-count analysis.
code_level_soft_ceiling_used_as_secondar.note: This is a SOFT, provider-token-budget-derived estimate, not observed real data - used only as an upper sanity bound to confirm the chosen MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_ROUND=12 is well below it (a genuine application-level tightening, not a restatement).
